subject: Stitch Gateway: access pattern tradeoffs (peering | PrivateLink | site-to-site VPN)
messages:
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Stitch Gateway: quick read on connectivity options for EdgeWorks

Team — attaching the partner brief from Stitch (attached) and a first-pass diagram from NetOps. EdgeWorks asked us to recommend one primary ingress pattern for their private deployment (they will run inference in their VPC and want low-latency, auditable access to Redwood Private).

High level ask from customer: "we want predictable latency, strict network isolation, and the ability to rotate keys on our side without rebuilding the tunnel". They also flagged that their VPC IP space overlaps with a handful of vendor networks (not terrible, but present).

Can each of you call out the risks and operational hit for Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN for this use case? My initial thinking below, but want a short bulleted POV we can pass to EWS NetOps and Stitch.

Initial bullets (for discussion):
- VPC peering: best raw latency, but fails if IP ranges overlap; needs cross-account route tables and careful egress controls. No service endpoint abstraction.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): good for access control (security groups), protects against IP overlap, but adds NAT/AWS-managed ENIs and per-GB charges; may have throughput/connection limits depending on the partner appliance.
- Site-to-site VPN: easiest on customer change control, supports overlapping IPs with NAT, but has worse latency variability, extra failure modes (BGP flaps, MTU issues), and more ops to rotate keys/certs.

Attachments: stitch-gateway-proposal.pdf (partner SLA and deployment modes), edgeworks-stitch-diagram-v1.png (customer network).

Thanks — please reply with 2–3 bullets each by EOD.

—Priyom

On Sun, 16 May 2027 at 09:12, priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — attaching the partner brief from Stitch (attached) and a first-pass diagram from NetOps. EdgeWorks asked us to recommend one primary ingress pattern for their private deployment (they will run inference in their VPC and want low-latency, auditable access to Redwood Private).
>
> Can each of you call out the risks and operational hit for Peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN for this use case? My initial thinking below, but want a short bulleted POV we can pass to EWS NetOps and Stitch.

Quick notes from infra side: (2–3 bullets)
- Peering: lowest P99 and simplest TCP path. But if EdgeWorks has overlapping CIDRs with any of the intermediate networks (e.g., a partner transit), we have to either ask them to re-IP or place a NAT gateway in front of the Redwood interface which adds latency and complexity. Peering also means cross-account route propagation — we need a small runbook for route changes and a verification checklist.
- PrivateLink: operationally clean for customers because it presents a service endpoint; avoids CIDR clash. However watch out for ENI quotas and potential multi-AZ failover semantics — test with >2k concurrent connections; Stitch's partner appliance must be proven for high QPS. Costs are predictable but can be higher per-GB. Also certificate rotation is simpler because TLS terminates at the endpoint, but we must ensure mTLS support end-to-end.
- S2S VPN: works as a fallback for NFC/regulatory customers. Support NAT-on-VPN if they insist on CIDR overlap. But expect jitter and lower throughput; MTU issues with fragmented tokens (large multipart requests) are a real pain — recommend TCP MSS clamping on the tunnel. For key rotation, prefer IKEv2 with automated certs (if they support it) to minimize scheduled downtime.

Operational asks for all options:
- Provide a standard runbook: failover test, smoke test (latency, tokens per second), and cost estimate.
- Add monitoring hooks: flow logs (ENI/VPC) + Redwood Console trace IDs to tie requests to network flows.

—Ben

Hi Priyom / Ben / Monica — thanks for the notes and for sharing the diagram. Quick clarifications from Stitch: we support three deployment modes for EdgeWorks: direct peering to our managed VPC, an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) backed by our appliance in customer subnets, or an S2S encrypted tunnel to our transit. Couple of points for the team to consider: 

- We can do mTLS passthrough for PrivateLink so customer's rotation remains local, but if EdgeWorks requires mutual auth inside their VPC we'd need to push a certificate agent to our appliance (we can script this).
- For peering, we recommend keeping the path single-hop (peering from EdgeWorks -> Stitch -> Redwood) instead of multi-transit to avoid asymmetric routing. Stitch can reserve a /28 for the peering arrangement to minimize overlap risk.
- VPN mode is our slowest option but can be useful for initial onboarding while teams finish IP renumbering. We offer automated rekeying for IKEv2 (no downtime expected in our tests) but you should still plan a rolling rekey schedule in the runbook.

I've attached the SLA and an example deploy timeline (stitch-gateway-proposal.pdf). Happy to join a call with EdgeWorks NetOps tomorrow morning if that helps.

Thanks — Rajesh
Stitch Gateway | Partner Integrations
rajesh@stitchgateway.com

Folks — short synthesis and recommended path for EdgeWorks.

Synthesis (3 bullets):
- If EdgeWorks can renumber or reserve a new /26 for the path, VPC peering gives the best latency and simplest debugging surface. Require a peering-only CIDR and shared runbook for route changes.
- If renumbering is not feasible, PrivateLink is the pragmatic primary: protects against CIDR overlap, simplifies access control (security groups + endpoint policies), and gives us a clear lifecycle boundary for audit logs. Ensure Stitch appliance supports the connection density required (ask for perf numbers at the requested QPS).
- Use S2S VPN as the onboarding/fallback path only. Add MSS clamping, BGP hold timers tuned, and a plan to migrate off VPN within the first 90 days.

Recommendation (one-line): Recommend PrivateLink as the default unless EdgeWorks commits to a new peering CIDR in the next 2 weeks; document S2S VPN as a temporary onboarding mode with a migration plan.

Operational checklist (short):
- Confirm CIDR overlap status and whether EdgeWorks can reserve a peering /26.
- Ask Stitch for ENI quotas, per-ENI throughput and NAT behavior, and a perf report at 95th p99 for 5000 TPS.
- Draft runbook: smoke test (connectivity + <200ms p95), cert rotation steps, fallback to VPN procedure, and monitoring dashboards (flow logs + Redwood trace ID).

If everyone agrees I will draft the one-pager to send to EdgeWorks NetOps and schedule the handoff call with Rajesh.

—Karthik
